assessment.governing_intent: Prove that the real sandbox_run_profile and github_profile constructors, using local transports, refuse multi-role worker launch when role authority, exact candidate custody or durable outcome correlation is missing or miscorrelated. A correctly bound real WorkerProvider must reach correlated success/rejection/restart readback through existing evidence ownership. No sidecar state owner is added and no live/shared-profile activation is claimed. The 2026-09-25 founder amendment also routes the worker-exit-without-durable-result incident (#94/#101/#110) into this BIU.
implementation_unknowns: Where in sandbox_run_profile and github_profile construction the binding guard should sit so it runs before any worker launch.

How the current WorkerOutcome and the invocation/effect/execution evidence records expose role, candidate and result correlation for the guard to check. The text says to extend WorkerOutcome only if Design Verification proves a required observable is missing.
How the real adapter can be exercised offline through local transports to produce success, rejection and restart readback without a mocked second lifecycle.
How supervised background work started by an invocation is currently tracked, and whether provider/client exit is already treated as terminal.
How FX-K3 should build each discriminating negative control: disconnected correlation, bypassed guard, missing custody, and premature ownership release.
material_risks: Scope creep: implementing replacement/recovery logic in K3 could cross into Execution Coordination orchestration that belongs to K2, or into the K1 readback seam.
Pressure to add RoleOutcomeRecord/OutcomeEvidencePort sidecar state if WorkerOutcome appears insufficient, which the text forbids unless separately reviewed.
The offline proof could use a test-specific lifecycle shortcut instead of the production composition path, which would invalidate the proof.
The completion predicate lists no founder-amendment behavior, so a verifier could accept a candidate that leaves the recurring incident unaddressed, or reject one for unstated criteria.
Predecessor DONE status and the pinned contract/baseline identities are reported but not independently verified by this gate. A source revision mismatch would trigger the task's own hold rule.
Accidental live/shared-profile activation from changes to profile constructors.
assessment.next_action: Have the owner (founder/BIU author) answer whether amendment recovery/replacement is a K3 implementation deliverable or a preserved-invariant proof. Then revise the completion predicate and proof plan with an observable failure class and negative control for it, or state an explicit non-claim deferring it to K1/K2's owner. After that, resubmit this exact revision for a fresh Agent Ready assessment.
owner_clarifications: Is implementing deterministic bounded recovery/replacement after conclusive invocation death (amendment bullet 2) a K3 deliverable? If yes, what observable acceptance should the completion predicate add, e.g. 'with ownership/effect state UNKNOWN no replacement launches; after confirmed death with missing durable result, exactly one replacement launches within attempt/budget policy'? Or does K3 only need to prove that the composed profiles preserve an existing K1/K2 recovery behavior?

Should the invocation-ownership-through-supervised-background-work invariant (amendment bullet 1) be satisfied in K3's composition/invocation scope, or does it touch K1's durable outcome/readback seam? If it touches K1's seam, should a discovered gap be escalated to K1's owner under the existing escalation rule rather than repaired in K3?
assessment.rationale: CLARIFY is the controlling condition because material owner intent about scope and acceptance is unresolved, not because engineering research remains. The binding guard alone would plausibly be READY: the predecessors are reported DONE, ownership is fixed, acceptance is observable and rework is bounded. The later amendment adds a behavioral obligation (deterministic recovery/replacement) that the acceptance criteria do not reflect. Whether K3 owns that behavior or K1/K2 owns it is a scope and architecture decision only the owner can make. SPLIT is not chosen because the owner explicitly routed the incident here, and the ownership-retention invariant is coupled to the same invocation/readback correlation the guard relies on. Separating it would be premature before the owner clarifies intent. HOLD is not chosen because no prerequisite is reported as unavailable.
assessment.summary: The core K3 extent is cohesive and verifiable. It adds a composition-level binding guard plus a proof, and its ownership boundaries, non-goals and negative-control policy are well specified. The founder amendment adds a second behavioral concern with two parts: (a) invocation ownership persists through supervised background work after the provider/client session exits, and (b) deterministic bounded recovery/replacement after conclusive invocation death with a confirmed missing durable result. The proof plan covers (a) as a material failure class. Neither the completion predicate nor any proof failure class covers (b). It is also unclear whether (b) is new behavior K3 must implement, or an existing K1/K2 behavior K3 must only not violate. That scope and acceptance ambiguity requires owner authority, so the task should not be handed off yet. The predecessor DONE status for K1 (WO-220401) and K2 (WO-220402) is reported in the text; this gate has not verified it.
assessment.verification_assessment: The binding-guard portion has observable acceptance: refusal before launch for each missing or miscorrelated binding, correlated readback for a correctly bound adapter, and proof failure when correlation is disconnected or the guard is bypassed. It has named test surfaces, an initial pytest command, and a one-negative-control-per-failure-class policy. One independent verifier verdict on the exact candidate SHA is meaningful for that portion. The ownership-retention failure class is also observable. The amendment's recovery/replacement behavior has no acceptance predicate or proof failure class, so a verifier cannot reach a coherent single verdict on the whole BIU until the owner decides whether it is in scope.
